summary: H.R. 2317, the Northern Nevada Economic Development and Conservation Act of 2026, directs the transfer, conveyance, sale, or disposal of specified federal lands in northern Nevada among federal agencies, the State of Nevada, local counties, cities, improvement districts, and a tribal nation. The bill designates multiple new wilderness areas, establishes land trust arrangements, releases federal reversionary interests in certain sites, provides for economic development and flood control conveyances, and authorizes a new federal office complex.

affected_groups.effect: Gain ownership of various federal lands for public purposes, economic development, parks, cemeteries, and flood control, while bearing associated survey, appraisal, and administrative costs.
affected_groups.group: State of Nevada and Local Governments (Counties and Cities)

affected_groups.effect: Receive federal and non-federal lands to be held in trust as part of their reservation, with authority to conduct fuel reduction and restoration activities.
affected_groups.group: Washoe Tribe of Nevada and California

affected_groups.effect: Subject to land withdrawals in designated wilderness and disposal areas, while qualified entities with encumbered land in Pershing County are offered opportunities to purchase remaining federal rights for fair market value.
affected_groups.group: Holders of Mining Claims and Encumbrances

key_provisions: Provides for the transfer and conveyance of federal lands from the Forest Service and Bureau of Land Management to the State of Nevada, local counties (Douglas, Clark, Pershing, Elko), and various cities for economic development, recreation, and public purposes.

Designates specific parcels of federal land as wilderness areas and components of the National Wilderness Preservation System, including the Burbank Canyons Wilderness and seven wilderness areas in Pershing County.
Takes specified land into trust for the Washoe Tribe of Nevada and California, while barring class II and class III gaming on those trust lands.

Releases the federal reversionary interest in the Jean Prison site, allowing the State of Nevada to use the land for purposes unrelated to the prison under specific aviation and airport development conditions.
Authorizes the Department of the Interior and the Forest Service to establish a joint federal office complex in Nevada using a portion of proceeds from land sales.
Authorizes land sales and exchanges in Pershing County to resolve historical railroad checkerboard land patterns and establishes special accounts to handle proceeds from land sales.

The bill designates multiple new wilderness areas, establishes land trust arrangements, releases federal reversionary interests in certain sites, provides for economic development and flood control conveyances, and authorizes a new federal office complex.
summary_detail.significance: The bill enacts comprehensive federal land management changes across multiple northern Nevada counties, altering ownership patterns for hundreds of thousands of acres through conveyances, sales, trust transfers, and wilderness designations. The score reflects a substantial geographic and legal scope affecting multiple jurisdictions, federal agencies, and local economies.
